episodes.156431: Severe storms producing 1-inch hail developed during the evening of April 15, impacting portions of Harris and Montgomery Counties.
episodes.156690: A quick, west to east zonal flow type pattern was present across the Southern Plains on April 16th, but weak perturbations embedded in this flow resulted in the necessary forcing to generate widespread showers and thunderstorms across the Four State Region. Cool temperatures aloft resulted in rather steep atmospheric lapse rates above a relatively cool and stable boundary layer, which proved the perfect ingredient for the development|of an isolated severe thunderstorm producing large hail in Natchitoches Parish in North Louisiana. As a result, quarter size hail was reported in the city of Robeline.
episodes.157877: A warm front was the focus for a couple of severe thunderstorms over the coastal waters. Those storms produced severe winds over the coastal waters.
episodes.157892: An apparent log jam developed on the Yalobusha River near Big Creek resulting in some lowland flooding south of the Big Creek Community. At least one home was flooded and County Road 312 was closed.
episodes.158111: A cut off upper low slowly worked across the deep south during the middle of April. This produced multiple days of stormy weather.
episodes.158112: A cut off low slowly moved across the Deep South and produced multiple days of stormy weather. A few storms became severe during the period.
